Kate.who: 34, woman, a teacher at the primary school

Gregory.who: 52, man, a teacher at the primary school

Anita.who: 41, woman, a teacher at the primary school

Anita.texts: You message the group quite often, mostly when something musical or lunchtime-related comes up.
Anita.style: some emoji and a few abbreviations

Noah.who: 27, man, a teacher at the primary school

Carol.who: 60, woman, a teacher at the primary school
Carol.knows: You know Kate as the literacy coordinator you collaborate with on reading programs, Gregory as the Year 6 teacher whose students borrow from your library, Anita as the music teacher who sometimes uses your song books, and Noah as the early-career teacher you help with book selections.

private_lines.Kate: You are the school's literacy coordinator, planning programs and supporting teachers across year levels, and you live in a family home in Perth's southern suburbs with your partner and two young children; mornings are busy with school runs, and weekday evenings are usually spent on dinner and the kids' reading.
private_lines.Gregory: You teach a Year 6 class at the primary school, spending your days on lesson planning, marking and assessment tracking, and you live in a house in Bassendean with your wife; you usually get up early to exercise before school and spend evenings reading or cooking.
private_lines.Anita: You teach music to classes across the school and run the choir and a lunchtime band, and you live alone in an apartment in Fremantle; your weekdays are full of rehearsals and practice, and weekends are often spent playing piano at a local church.
private_lines.Noah: You are an early-career classroom teacher spending your days on planning, marking and catching up after school, and you rent a unit in Mount Lawley; you go to the gym a few evenings a week and see friends on weekends.
private_lines.Carol: You are the school's library and reading coordinator, looking after the collection and running reading events, and you live alone in a family home in Nedlands with a garden you tend most mornings; on weekends you volunteer at a local library and take long walks.
